subject.title: build(deps): remove npm shrinkwrap; mirror pnpm lock into transient package locks

question: Should OpenClaw accept install-time transitive dependency resolution for the root package and native-heavy plugin opt-outs now that npm shrinkwrap is unavailable, while retaining bundling for the other publishable plugins?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the shipped supply-chain and upgrade contract; source review can establish mechanics, but the acceptable release-security tradeoff requires owner intent.

options.title: Accept the replacement contract
options.body: Approve the lockless root/native-opt-out model after reviewing the npm 12 package, upgrade, and provenance evidence for the exact merge head.

options.title: Require stronger package containment
options.body: Pause this PR until the root package and affected opt-out plugins have an approved publish-time bundling or equivalent reproducibility design.

options.title: Defer the migration
options.body: Keep shrinkwrap-dependent release behavior only if an owner confirms a supported npm compatibility path remains viable.

recommendation.title: Accept the replacement contract
recommendation.body: Approve the lockless root/native-opt-out model after reviewing the npm 12 package, upgrade, and provenance evidence for the exact merge head.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the migration and are identified in the dependency-graph guard as a trusted secops actor, so they are the best available person to route the intended package-security contract to the appropriate owners.
